correctness.rationale: An invertible affine change preserves all attainable phase pairs, and the common translation phase cancels from orthogonality. For two normalized characters the zero condition is a+bz=-(c+dz)w with z,w on the unit circle. Equality of the two magnitudes gives H+2J Re(z)=0, also sufficient when both sides vanish. Four characters fill the four-dimensional weighted evaluation space; squared row norms are four times the masses, so four are possible exactly at uniformity. For a triple the three-column projection similarly gives 3 times each mass <=1. If H=J=0, equality of the sums and products of the positive row pairs leaves either a zero line w=-1 (if a=c and b=d with a!=b, ruling out a triple) or the opposite-equal case a=d, b=c. There the projection bound is the stated ratio-two bound; the cosine construction cancels the first two differences by C plus the reciprocal-ratio term, and the third by 2C^2-1=-r, valid including r=1/2 and after swapping the roles of a,b. Outside H=J=0 the denominator can vanish at a zero only when z=-1, a=b and c=d; its zero line likewise precludes a triple. Otherwise Re(z) is fixed and w determined, so the zeros are contained in a conjugate pair. A triple must have a nonidentity order-three difference, because both opposite points and their doubled difference must also be zeros. Strict positivity rules out either coordinate equal to 1 at order three. The only possible phase pairs then impose a=d=b+c or b=c=a+d via the real relation 1+omega+omega^2=0, each attained. Uniformity is correctly checked first. `python3 /workspace/review_replay.py 3` independently checked representative cube-root witnesses and ratio-two boundary identities in exact arithmetic; the case proof covers all real masses, not only sampled weights.
residual_risks: The support must be a nondegenerate parallelogram with strictly positive masses. The proof gives maximum cardinality with real frequencies, not all inclusion-maximal systems or results for integer-only frequencies.

evidence: The tetrahedron result has the same two-equal-pair weights and inclusive ratio [1/2,2] for triples off uniformity, but independent coordinates supply all four phases up to a common phase. The square imposes phase(00)*phase(11)=phase(10)*phase(01). Theorem 3 for two parallel segments requires equal constant densities for full spectrality.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Tetrahedral impossibility applies to the restricted square phases, but tetrahedral existence does not imply existence under the extra phase relation. Continuous segment spectrality does not govern partial orthogonality among four positive point masses.

Neither the planar no-other-triples statement nor the opposite-equal sufficiency follows from these sources: failure on one phase subtorus is not failure on the full torus, and a tetrahedral witness is not automatically a parallelogram witness. The support is not a spectrally equivalent affine model for the entire planar frequency domain.

originality.rationale: Meaningful subcases are covered or bounded by related theorems, including the existence of the two root-of-unity families from the one-dimensional classification by projection and reflection. The distinct result is the full classification on the phase-constrained parallelogram, in particular attainability throughout the opposite-equal interval under its phase constraint and the exhaustive exclusion of any other triples.

value.rationale: The smallest planar parallelogram carries both a nontrivial dependence among the four phases and varying positive atom masses. The exact classification distinguishes existence of one zero from packing three pairwise-orthogonal characters, and exhibits both a sharp continuous threshold and isolated types of torsion resonance. Having the exhaustion on the full torus is useful and is not a restatement of finite spectrality or either related support classification.
residual_risks: No general planar quadrilateral classification or complete parametrization of all maximizing frequency families is obtained.
